shortDescription: Advanced Innergy Holdings ASX:AIH expects earnings to recover in the 2027 financial year after acquisitions helped lift annual revenue by 10.8% to A$331.6 million (£166.8m) despite disruption from the Middle East conflict.The materials science specialist finished September with a record order book…

children: Advanced Innergy Holdings
expects earnings to recover in the 2027 financial year after acquisitions helped lift annual revenue by 10.8% to A$331.6 million (£166.8m) despite disruption from the Middle East conflict.

The materials science specialist finished September with a record order book of A$328m (£165m), up 55% on the previous year and incorporating its acquisitions of Imenco Aqua and Matrix Composites & Engineering.
Underlying EBITDA nevertheless fell 16.6% to A$46.3m (£23.3m), as delays to project delivery and rising supply costs weighed on profitability.
Underlying net profit after tax and before amortisation of acquired intangibles also declined 26.6% to A$19.3m (£9.7m), while statutory NPAT fell 82.6% to A$3.7m (£1.853m).

The company expects both revenue and underlying EBITDA to exceed the latest annual results, supported by a recovering market and a more balanced distribution of project deliveries throughout the year.
Ongoing Margin Pressure

Acquisitions accounted for much of the revenue increase in the year to 30 September, with organic revenue remaining broadly stable as customers took longer to progress procurement on awarded projects.

Gross profit margins declined from 36.3% to 34.1% as the company delivered two lower-margin legacy contracts and absorbed higher input costs that it could not immediately pass on to customers under fixed-price agreements.

“Although FY26 organic performance fell short of our expectations, we took several decisive actions during the year which leaves us well positioned to capitalise on future opportunities in our various markets,” chief executive officer Andrew Bennion said.

“Overall, we remain optimistic for the outlook of AIH, particularly given the heightened global focus on sovereign energy security which we see as a key catalyst for new and accelerated project development in the longer term.”
Matrix Integration Synergies
Advanced Innergy has increased its estimate of potential annual synergies from the July acquisition of Matrix to approximately A$23.9m (£12m), around 70% above its original expectations.
The company anticipates realising up to a quarter of the annual benefit in the current financial year, with the full run rate expected by the 2029 financial year.

The acquisition expands the group’s subsea buoyancy product range and manufacturing capacity, with the combined business already winning a joint contract that incorporates Matrix design expertise and Advanced Innergy technology.

Matrix’s supplier network has opened alternative sources of key raw materials, while the March acquisition of Imenco Aqua has extended the Marine segment’s aquaculture operations into Norway and Chile.
Cash Flow Recovery Target

The Subsea segment accounted for 56% of annual revenue, with the Thermal and Marine businesses contributing 30% and 14% respectively as the company broadened its exposure to markets beyond oil and gas.

New commercial opportunities include a framework agreement for subsea telecommunications cable protection, battery thermal protection work with a global carmaker and fire protection products for data centre fuel tanks.
Operating cash flow fell to A$2.8m (£1.4m) from A$48.9m (£24.6m), reflecting lower earnings and a deliberate increase in inventory to counter supply chain disruption.
Net debt increased to A$136.6m (£68.7m) following acquisitions and higher working capital requirements.

Advanced Innergy expects operating cash flow conversion to exceed 100% of EBITDA in the current financial year as it releases working capital, with net leverage progressively declining below two times.

title: Advanced Innergy Eyes FY27 Earnings Recovery After Order Book Surges to Record
